content:
Over the past couple of days, two reports have separately suggested different ways Apple could make more money by increasing services revenue.

In my view, Apple should absolutely do the former, but not the latter – and it seems Phil Schiller may well agree …

First, let me summarize the two reports.

Home security and monitoring service

On Friday, Bloomberg revealed that Apple may be planning to launch a brand new home security and monitoring service, designed to work with some of the new home hardware products we are already expecting.

Squeezing more money from the App Store

A second report from the same source on Sunday suggested that Apple is exploring ways to squeeze more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple shouldn't take the latter approach

I believe the second approach would be a very serious mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly position on iPhone app sales has come under heavy fire from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell iPhone apps, you're forced to go through the official App Store – you have no choice at all, you must accept Apple's terms, with zero negotiating power.

I understand many will say nobody is forcing you to buy an iPhone or develop apps for it, but that's not how genuine laissez-faire capitalism works: even in the US, there have been anti-monopoly laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, there are restrictions in place to make sure you don't abuse that position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store runs completely counter to the idea of skating to where the puck is going, and Schiller is reportedly of the same view, with Bloomberg saying this was one of the reasons he chose to step down from his current role.

Innovative services are the right direction

By contrast, launching innovative services that people pay to use voluntarily is what Apple should be doing. I can absolutely see the value of this company offering a home security monitoring service.

Back in 2024, I said launching its own smart home cameras would be one of the smartest moves the company could make. The same goes for the rumored Apple smart doorbell. Offering an optional service bundle for security products makes complete sense, for two reasons.

First, there are the various privacy reasons I mentioned before. HomeKit Secure Video has already done a great deal to protect the privacy of security camera footage. If there's one company I would trust to perform AI analysis on security camera footage, it's Apple.

Second, Apple is of course the company best placed to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit ecosystem. I'm sure there are many other areas where Apple could offer similar benefits.

For me, the point is that Apple needs to apply the same attitude to services as it does to hardware – making great products that people willingly and happily pay to use, rather than making money in ways that annoy customers, developers, and regulators alike.

What do you think about this? Please share your views in the comments section.
